title: GovEagle adds formatting awareness to the Word add-in
summary: The GovEagle Word add-in now reads bold, italic, underlined, struck-through and colored text in your document, and inserts real Word tables.
body_markdown:
The GovEagle Word add-in now reads the formatting in your document and inserts real Word tables.


## What changed


Proposal teams use formatting to carry meaning: bold for compliance language, color for reviewer notes, strikethrough for text on its way out. Now:


- **GovEagle sees it.** The add-in reads bold, italic, underlined, struck-through and colored text.
- **You can ask about it.** Try "List every sentence in red text" or "Are all the bolded shall statements addressed?"
- **Real Word tables.** When GovEagle suggests a table, it inserts a true Word table, not lines of pipe characters.


## Who it helps


Proposal writers and reviewers working through color-team comments in Word, and anyone who has cleaned up a pasted table by hand.


## How it works


1. Open your document and the GovEagle add-in in Word.
2. Ask a question that depends on formatting, or ask for a table.
3. Apply the suggested edits, or turn on Auto-accept to have them inserted for you.


Get GovCon capture and proposal insights in your inbox.


## Where it fits


The Word add-in is part of[GovEagle's proposal tools](https://www.goveagle.com/solutions/proposals) . For how it compares with other options, read[the best Microsoft Word add-ins for government proposal writing](https://www.goveagle.com/blog/microsoft-word-addins-government-proposal-writing) .


## What it doesn't do


- **It reads text color, not highlighter shading.** Ask about "text in red," not "highlighted in red."
- **It doesn't decide what the formatting means.** Tell GovEagle what your colors stand for.
